text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government reshuffle expected in the last week of May.

- During Yugoslav-Macedonian border demarcation talks Macedonia said it would claim the territory of Monastery of St Prohor Pcinjski which is now in Yugoslavia. Foundations for the Macedonian state were established in that monastery on August 2, 1944.
- Tome Nenovski, Vice-Governor of the National Bank of Macedonia was released from custody in Skopje Tuesday after posting a 415,000 German mark bail.

- Prime Minister Branko Crvenkovski will meet VMRO-DPMNE leader Ljubco Goergievski on Wednesday. The meeting marks the start of dialogue between leading political parties for preparation of the new electoral laws.
- VMRO-DPMNE will hold its postponed protest on May 15 at 1800 local time under the slogan "Halt to economic, social and state collapse of Macedonia", said party leader Ljubco Georgievski.

- The World Bank on Tuesday approved a $60 million loan to Macedonia, $30 million of which is a credit approved under conditions of the International Development Associations (IDA). -- Mircela Casule, Skopje newsroom +389 91 201 196
